cases.sentence: Первое время своего пребывания в Петербурге, князь Андрей почувствовал весь свой склад мыслей, выработавшийся в его уединенной жизни, совершенно затемненным теми ___, которые охватили его в Петербурге.
cases.explain: «мелкими заботами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: During the first weeks of his stay in Petersburg Prince Andréy felt the whole trend of thought he had formed during his life of seclusion quite overshadowed by the trifling cares that engrossed him in that city.

cases.sentence: С вечера, возвращаясь домой, он в памятной книжке записывал четыре или пять ___ или rendez-vous[487] свиданий в назначенные часы.
cases.explain: «необходимых визитов» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: On returning home in the evening he would jot down in his notebook four or five necessary calls or appointments for certain hours. The mechanism of life, the arrangement of the day so as to be in time everywhere, absorbed the greater part of his vital energy. He did nothing, did not even think or find time to think, but only talked, and talked successfully, of what he had thought while in the country.

cases.sentence: Он иногда замечал с неудовольствием, что ему случалось в один и тот же день, в ___, повторять одно и то же.
cases.explain: «разных обществах» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: He sometimes noticed with dissatisfaction that he repeated the same remark on the same day in different circles. But he was so busy for whole days together that he had no time to notice that he was thinking of nothing.

cases.sentence: Этот первый, длинный разговор с Сперанским только усилил в князе Андрее то чувство, с которым он в ___ увидал Сперанского.
cases.explain: «первый раз» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: This first long conversation with Speránski only strengthened in Prince Andréy the feeling he had experienced toward him at their first meeting. He saw in him a remarkable, clear-thinking man of vast intellect who by his energy and persistence had attained power, which he was using solely for the welfare of Russia. In Prince Andréy’s eyes Speránski was the man he would himself have wished to be—one who explained all the facts of life reasonably, considered important only what was rational, and was capable of applying the standard of reason to everything. Everything seemed so simple and clear in Speránski’s exposition that Prince Andréy involuntarily agreed with him about everything. If he replied and argued, it was only because he wished to maintain his independence and not submit to Speránski’s opinions entirely. Everything was right and everything was as it should be: only one thing disconcerted Prince Andréy. This was Speránski’s cold, mirrorlike look, which did not allow one to penetrate to his soul, and his delicate white hands, which Prince Andréy involuntarily watched as one does watch the hands of those who possess power. This mirrorlike gaze and those delicate hands irritated Prince Andréy, he knew not why. He was unpleasantly struck, too, by the excessive contempt for others that he observed in Speránski, and by the diversity of lines of argument he used to support his opinions. He made use of every kind of mental device, except analogy, and passed too boldly, it seemed to Prince Andréy, from one to another. Now he would take up the position of a practical man and condemn dreamers; now that of a satirist, and laugh ironically at his opponents; now grow severely logical, or suddenly rise to the realm of metaphysics.

cases.sentence: Он видел в нем разумного, строго-мыслящего, ___ человека, энергией и упорством достигшего власти и употребляющего ее только для блага России.

cases.sentence: Зеркальный взгляд и ___ эта почему-то раздражали князя Андрея.
cases.explain: «нежная рука» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: (This last resource was one he very frequently employed.) He would transfer a question to metaphysical heights, pass on to definitions of space, time, and thought, and, having deduced the refutation he needed, would again descend to the level of the original discussion.

cases.sentence: То он становился на почву ___ и осуждал мечтателей, то на почву сатирика и иронически подсмеивался над противниками, то становился строго логичным, то вдруг поднимался в область метафизики.
cases.explain: «практического деятеля» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: (This last resource was one he very frequently employed.) He would transfer a question to metaphysical heights, pass on to definitions of space, time, and thought, and, having deduced the refutation he needed, would again descend to the level of the original discussion.

cases.sentence: Вообще ___ ума Сперанского, поразившая князя Андрея, была несомненная, непоколебимая вера в силу и законность ума.
cases.explain: «главная черта» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: In general the trait of Speránski’s mentality which struck Prince Andréy most was his absolute and unshakable belief in the power and authority of reason. It was evident that the thought could never occur to him which to Prince Andréy seemed so natural, namely, that it is after all impossible to express all one thinks; and that he had never felt the doubt, “Is not all I think and believe nonsense?” And it was just this peculiarity of Speránski’s mind that particularly attracted Prince Andréy.

cases.sentence: Вообще главная черта ума Сперанского, поразившая князя Андрея, была несомненная, ___ в силу и законность ума.

cases.sentence: Князь Андрей сказал, что для этого нужно ___, которого он не имеет.
cases.explain: «юридическое образование» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Prince Andréy said that for that work an education in jurisprudence was needed which he did not possess.

cases.sentence: Через неделю князь Андрей был членом комиссии составления ___, и, чего он никак не ожидал, начальником отделения комиссии составления законов.
cases.explain: «воинского устава» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: A week later Prince Andréy was a member of the Committee on Army Regulations and—what he had not at all expected—was chairman of a section of the committee for the revision of the laws. At Speránski’s request he took the first part of the Civil Code that was being drawn up and, with the aid of the Code Napoléon and the Institutes of Justinian, he worked at formulating the section on Personal Rights.

cases.sentence: По просьбе Сперанского он взял первую часть составляемого ___ и, с помощию Code Napoléon и Justiniani,[489] Наполеоновского кодекса и кодекса Юстиниана, работал над составлением отдела: Права лиц.
